args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest production deploy) was failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc had also been marked unhealthy. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After rollback: all regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate ~0.2%. Follow-up: investigate v2.3.1 regression and why it was promoted despite an unhealthy staging RC.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, the service is healthy again, and I opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was the latest deploy and was failing in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%. The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0, so all three regions are now running that.
- **Check afterwards:** checkout-api reports healthy on v2.3.0 everywhere, with an error rate of about 0.2%. No change-manager approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 as a SEV2 for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the health after the rollback.

The test version of v2.3.1 was already marked unhealthy in staging before v2.3.1 went to production. The incident lists that as a follow-up to look into, along with the v2.3.1 failure itself.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
